conversion_pathway.process: Riboflavin supplies the precursor for FMN used by complex I.
conversion_pathway.limitations: The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context. The sources are reviews of enzyme structure and function, not human feeding trials. Flavin mononucleotide (FMN) abundance has not been shown to limit complex I in ordinary conditions. Endogenous ubiquinone synthesis is not separated here from dietary coenzyme Q10. Copper and iron centres are not evidence that supplements raise chain activity.

conversion_pathway.process: Riboflavin supplies the precursor for FMN used by complex I.
conversion_pathway.limitations: The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context. The sources are reviews of enzyme structure and function, not human feeding trials. Flavin mononucleotide (FMN) abundance has not been shown to limit complex I in ordinary conditions. Endogenous ubiquinone synthesis is not separated here from dietary coenzyme Q10. Copper and iron centres are not evidence that supplements raise chain activity.

evidence.statement: Riboflavin is the vitamin precursor of flavin mononucleotide (FMN), the flavin that accepts NADH electrons in complex I.

limitations: The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context.

conversion_pathway.process: Multistep hepatic kynurenine/de-novo NAD metabolism and subsequent nicotinamide availability for salvage; not a direct one-step tryptophan-to-nicotinamide reaction.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺. This is a review of pathways, not a human feeding trial. It does not measure how much an ordinary meal changes NAD⁺, and it does not test attention or cognitive energy. Nicotinamide riboside and nicotinamide mononucleotide, as supplement doses, are outside this dietary assessment.

manuscript_rows.biological_mechanism: Enable mitochondrial ketone utilisation so alternative fuel is available when glucose conditions shift.
manuscript_rows.food_material: unheated commercial St. Francis Herb Farm C8/C10 MCT oil from a health-food store; formulation-dependent

food_evidence.evidence: Kosarac et al. (2021), Frontiers in Chemistry 9:756745, unheated MCT oil, Table 1; ABITEC CAPTEX product identity
food_evidence.limitations: Identified in a studied commercial C8/C10 MCT oil; content depends on the formulation and a separate amount is unavailable.

conversion_pathway.process: Digestive lipolysis releases C8 fatty acid from trioctanoin; the absorbed fatty acid is represented as octanoate at physiological pH.
conversion_pathway.limitations: The C8 acyl form is not free octanoate content in food. Mixed-chain MCT products have formulation-dependent composition.

evidence.statement: Human triglyceride-lipase reaction provenance and the defined oral tricaprylin exposure; retrieved 26 October 2026.

conversion_pathway.process: Hepatic fatty-acid activation and successive mitochondrial beta-oxidation reactions generate acetyl-CoA from the C8 chain.
conversion_pathway.limitations: This is a multireaction biological process, not a single chemical reaction. Tissue partitioning and energy state prevent a fixed food-to-acetyl-CoA yield. Cofactor participation creates no separate dietary admissions.

evidence.statement: Human medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase establishes the initial beta-oxidation reaction; the clinical exposure additionally measures downstream ketone provision.

conversion_pathway.process: Hepatic mitochondrial ketogenesis proceeds through acetoacetyl-CoA formation, HMG-CoA synthase and HMG-CoA lyase to produce acetoacetate.
dependencies: Ketone release, circulation and brain monocarboxylate transport
conversion_pathway.limitations: The endogenous product can interconvert with beta-hydroxybutyrate, but the target identity here is acetoacetate. Ketogenesis, cerebral uptake and ATP production are distinct; no fixed yield or universal benefit is inferred.

evidence.statement: Curated human ACAT1, HMGCS2 and HMGCL reactions, retrieved 26 October 2026.

limitations: Uncontrolled sequential exposure: C8/C10 mixture (n=11) then 95% tricaprylin (n=6), 30 g/day for one month each. No claim of isolated C8 superiority, cognitive efficacy, healthy-person requirement or ordinary coconut-oil equivalence. PET uptake/metabolism is not a direct cellular ATP assay; no food-effective dose or fixed conversion yield is inferred.

functional_dependency.statement: Copper supplies the CuA/CuB centres required for complex-IV electron transfer and oxygen reduction. Dietary copper deficiency impairs cardiac cytochrome-c-oxidase capacity in rats.

Endogenous phenylalanine conversion is an alternative source; the full human intervening enzyme sequence remains incompletely assigned.

functional_dependency.statement: Tyrosine supplies quinone-head carbon through the HPDL-associated 4-HMA/4-HB pathway.

dietary_supply.statement: Existing canonical food composition records establish dietary provision of this named nutrient, independently of its CoQ role.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Reused existing amino-acid, riboflavin and iron composition records with original food-state and measurement provenance. No food is claimed to supply a mitochondrial dose or contain the downstream intracellular product because of precursor presence. No new nutrient concentration is inferred.

conversion_pathway.process: Tyrosine-derived headgroup carbon enters CoQ10 through 4-HPP, HPDL-associated 4-HMA and 4-HB formation followed by prenylation and COQ maturation; this is a net precursor relationship, not an assertion that all intervening human enzymes are assigned.

functional_dependency.statement: The liver can convert tryptophan to nicotinamide, which other cells salvage into NAD⁺.

dietary_supply.statement: The liver can convert tryptophan to nicotinamide, which other cells salvage into NAD⁺.

conversion_pathway.process: Multistep hepatic kynurenine/de-novo NAD metabolism and subsequent nicotinamide availability for salvage; not a direct one-step tryptophan-to-nicotinamide reaction.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺. This is a review of pathways, not a human feeding trial. It does not measure how much an ordinary meal changes NAD⁺, and it does not test attention or cognitive energy. Nicotinamide riboside and nicotinamide mononucleotide, as supplement doses, are outside this dietary assessment.

food_target_research.sufficient_coverage_rationale: Inspected MCT Oil’s analytical product-specific triglyceride relationship and Coconut Oil’s explicit distinction between fatty-acid composition and individual triglycerides. functional_dependency.statement: Defined dietary caprylic triglyceride can supply hepatic ketone production and cerebral ketone-fuel availability for this ketone-utilisation operation.

dietary_supply.statement: The primary experiment used an orally administered tricaprylin-rich preparation. The MCT Oil record has a product/preparation-dependent caprylic-triglyceride relationship; fatty-acid content alone is not proof of trioctanoin content.

conversion_pathway.process: Digestive lipolysis releases C8 fatty acid from trioctanoin; the absorbed fatty acid is represented as octanoate at physiological pH.
conversion_pathway.limitations: The C8 acyl form is not free octanoate content in food. Mixed-chain MCT products have formulation-dependent composition.

evidence.statement: Human triglyceride-lipase reaction provenance and the defined oral tricaprylin exposure; retrieved 26 October 2026.

conversion_pathway.process: Hepatic fatty-acid activation and successive mitochondrial beta-oxidation reactions generate acetyl-CoA from the C8 chain.
conversion_pathway.limitations: This is a multireaction biological process, not a single chemical reaction. Tissue partitioning and energy state prevent a fixed food-to-acetyl-CoA yield. Cofactor participation creates no separate dietary admissions.

evidence.statement: Human medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase establishes the initial beta-oxidation reaction; the clinical exposure additionally measures downstream ketone provision.

conversion_pathway.process: Hepatic mitochondrial ketogenesis proceeds through acetoacetyl-CoA formation, HMG-CoA synthase and HMG-CoA lyase to produce acetoacetate.
dependencies: Ketone release, circulation and brain monocarboxylate transport
conversion_pathway.limitations: The endogenous product can interconvert with beta-hydroxybutyrate, but the target identity here is acetoacetate. Ketogenesis, cerebral uptake and ATP production are distinct; no fixed yield or universal benefit is inferred.

evidence.statement: Curated human ACAT1, HMGCS2 and HMGCL reactions, retrieved 26 October 2026.
